recent_posts.title: GitHub's reliability crisis and the role of AI-driven growth
recent_posts.summary: GitHub's reliability has deteriorated sharply, with 257 incidents tracked between May 2025 and April 2026, including 48 major outages. GitHub Actions alone suffered 57 outages in that period. The root cause, per GitHub's CTO, is the explosive growth of agentic AI workflows demanding 30x the platform's designed capacity. High-profile users like Mitchell Hashimoto (Ghostty) and the Zig project have migrated away. Compounding the scaling crisis are engineering failures like an incomplete feature flag that silently reverted thousands of merged pull requests. Microsoft's absorption of GitHub into its CoreAI org and commercial pressure around Copilot are seen as contributing factors. GitHub has declared an 'availability first' mandate, but community patience is running thin as comparable platforms like GitLab and npm handle the same AI-driven growth without comparable disruptions.

recent_posts.title: Enterprise AI agents leak sensitive data at rates up to 51% study finds
recent_posts.summary: A new study using the CI-Work benchmark of 125 simulated enterprise tasks finds that frontier LLM agents leak sensitive corporate data at rates between 16% and 51%. The core problem is that LLMs cannot distinguish task-relevant information from contextually inappropriate data when retrieving from sources like Slack, emails, and meeting transcripts. Counterintuitively, more capable models and more thorough retrieval instructions worsen privacy violations. Researchers conclude that models cannot self-police: engineering teams must implement least-privilege access controls, context-aware filtering, and audit logs before data reaches the model's prompt window. The safest enterprise agent is not the most capable model but the best-constrained system.

recent_posts.title: Coinbase flattens management and trims workforce in AI-driven restructure
recent_posts.summary: Coinbase is cutting 14% of its global workforce and flattening its management structure to a maximum of five layers below CEO/COO. CEO Brian Armstrong cites both the crypto market downturn and an AI-first strategic shift as drivers. The company is replacing traditional managers with 'player-coaches' who are also individual contributors, and plans to create 'AI-native pods' — potentially single-person teams directing AI agents that cover engineering, design, and product roles. Industry CTOs quoted in the piece broadly agree that AI is reducing the need for organizational layers by expanding the context individuals can hold, though the move follows a broader trend of tech companies linking layoffs to AI-driven efficiency.

recent_posts.title: How technical interviews are evolving in the age of AI
recent_posts.summary: Technical interviews are evolving but not dying as AI reshapes software development. LeetCode-style algorithmic questions persist at major companies, with 0 out of 52 FAANG interviewers having dropped them entirely, though over half have adjusted question types. Startups are moving faster — 67% say AI has meaningfully changed their process versus 0% at FAANG firms. Meta has added an AI-assisted coding stage, widening problem scope and exposing candidates to full codebases. Assessment criteria are shifting toward reviewing and debugging AI-generated code, system design, technical judgment, and handling ambiguity. Interview coaching firms are adapting by adding AI-assisted coding training, and demand for coaching may actually increase as AI levels the coding playing field and technical assessments expand beyond engineering roles.

recent_posts.title: Why DORA metrics give false confidence in the age of AI coding
recent_posts.summary: DORA metrics measure delivery throughput but not system comprehension, and AI-generated code is widening that gap. As AI tools accelerate deployment frequency and reduce change failure rates on paper, teams may lose genuine understanding of their critical systems. The author argues that DORA's blind spots include out-of-band changes from vendors, AI agents, and identity providers that never enter the traditional SDLC review process. Practical recommendations include adding detailed scope notes to DORA reviews, requiring incident narratives alongside metrics, and testing whether team members can explain critical paths end-to-end. The core message: DORA is a scoped instrument, not a complete health signal, and leaders must stop treating it as one.

recent_posts.title: The reality of being a senior engineering manager
recent_posts.summary: The transition from engineering manager to senior engineering manager is less about managing larger teams and more about shaping the systems and environments in which execution happens. Senior EMs must operate through influence rather than authority, building trust across organizational boundaries, aligning stakeholders without formal power, and coaching leaders rather than individual contributors. Key distinctions include: impact defined by organizational scope not org size, invisible work like pre-aligning stakeholders and resolving misaligned incentives, maintaining technical depth at a higher altitude to make system-level bets, and using directors to amplify systems rather than rescue them. The role also evolves in the context of AI-native systems, where senior EMs increasingly act as integrators across people, platforms, and intelligent systems. The core shift is moving from personal execution excellence to ensuring the entire system executes well.

recent_posts.title: Four practices that compound into lasting software engineering career growth
recent_posts.summary: A 16-year software engineering veteran shares four compounding practices for career growth: deliberate writing and documentation, building community, structured experimentation, and managing imposter syndrome. Drawing from experience across IT service firms, product companies, and a startup, the author argues that technical excellence alone is insufficient. Key insights include keeping a personal learning log, using code reviews as learning tools, blocking unstructured exploration time, and reframing imposter syndrome as something to manage rather than eliminate.

recent_posts.title: How Cloudflare rebuilt Next.js in a weekend using agentic coding
recent_posts.summary: Cloudflare rebuilt Next.js in a single weekend using Claude in OpenCode, spending just $1,100 in tokens. The result, called vinext, is a Vite plugin that reimplements the Next.js API surface natively for Cloudflare's infrastructure. It builds production apps up to 4x faster and produces 57% smaller client bundles. Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht frames this as the next evolution of open-source forking, made dramatically cheaper and faster by agentic coding. He argues the build-vs-buy equation has fundamentally changed, shifting engineers from writing code to directing AI agents through plans and specs. While not every team should rebuild everything, Knecht believes agentic coding will spur a wave of purpose-built replacements for aging open-source projects.

recent_posts.title: Six software engineering buzzwords to replace with precise language
recent_posts.summary: Six overused software engineering buzzwords are examined and critiqued: 'AI-powered', '10x engineer', 'tech debt', 'vibe coding', 'velocity', and 'shift left'. Each term is analyzed for how it lost precision and became counterproductive, with input from senior engineers and engineering leaders. Concrete replacements are suggested for each — for example, replacing 'AI-powered' with specific technique and outcome descriptions, '10x engineer' with 'high-leverage engineer', and 'shift left' with explicit, actionable language like 'test earlier' or 'flag security issues before code review'. The core argument is that vague buzzwords widen the gap between technical and business stakeholders rather than bridging it, and that precise language leads to better decision-making.

recent_posts.title: AI coding tool costs are rising as agentic usage explodes
recent_posts.summary: AI coding tool costs are rising sharply as agentic workflows consume far more tokens than traditional chat-based interactions. Vendors like GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, and Windsurf have moved from flat subscriptions to token-based billing, introduced usage multipliers, and tightened rate limits. Internal data suggests GitHub Copilot's serving costs have nearly doubled since January 2025. Engineering managers now face a choice between absorbing higher cloud AI costs or shifting to local LLM inference, while also needing to justify AI spend with concrete ROI rather than anecdotal productivity gains.
